tools.name: list_workouts
tools.description: List recorded rides, newest first, one compact row each: date, program mode, duration, distance, average power and heart rate. Use this first to find the id of a ride before asking for its detail. Optional filters: `from` and `to` (dates), `machineType`, `mode`; `limit` caps the rows. Returns no sample series.

tools.name: get_workout
tools.description: Everything derived about one ride, by `id` (from list_workouts; either id form works): duration, distance, work done, average and peak power, cadence and resistance, heart rate's average, minimum and maximum both as the console reported them and as the filtered series gives them, and what the console was actually holding constant — with the resistance metrics behind that call, because the series alone does not always settle it. Does not return the sample series — use get_samples for that.

id.description: Workout id, from list_workouts. Either id form works.

tools.name: get_samples
tools.description: The raw interval series for one ride as CSV — power, cadence, resistance, heart rate, speed, one row per 10 seconds. A full ride is several hundred rows, so a window or stride that would exceed the row limit is downsampled to fit, never cut short; the note under the CSV says when that happened. Takes the ride's `id`; optionally `fields`, a window (`fromSeconds`, `toSeconds`), a stride as `everyNth` or `resolutionSeconds`, and `maxRows`.

id.description: Workout id, from list_workouts. Either id form works.

everyNth.description: Stride; 6 gives one row per minute.

resolutionSeconds.description: The stride in seconds instead, a multiple of 10; 60 gives one row per minute.

tools.name: summarize_history
tools.description: Training volume per week or month — rides, time, distance, work, average power and heart rate — plus the all-time power curve over the matched rides. Takes the same date, machine and mode filters as list_workouts, and both the totals and the curve are computed over what matched, so filter by mode to keep a Sprint 8's spikes out of a steady-state summary. Arguments: `from`, `to`, `machineType`, `mode`, `bucket` (week or month) and `windowsSeconds` for the power curve, all optional. This is the tool for questions about trends, totals and bests.

windowsSeconds.description: Power-curve durations in seconds, multiples of 10. Default 10, 30, 60, 300, 600, 1200, 3600.

tools.name: compare_workouts
tools.description: Two or more rides side by side on every derived number, given as `ids` (two to eight, from list_workouts). Use it for 'how did today compare to last Tuesday' rather than calling get_workout repeatedly.

ids.description: Two to eight workout ids, from list_workouts.

tools.name: export_workout
tools.description: Write one ride to disk as a lossless JSON export document — normalized telemetry plus the upstream record verbatim. Takes the ride's `id` and an optional `path`. Returns the path written, not the contents, because the document is far too large to read into a conversation.

id.description: Workout id, from list_workouts. Either id form works.

path.description: Directory or file path. Defaults to the cache directory.

tools.name: refresh_history
tools.description: Re-download the whole history from the API, replacing the cache. Takes no arguments. Needs credentials. Everything else answers from the cache, so call this only when a ride is missing because it happened since the last fetch.
